briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 18, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Stalemate in Global Climate Governance and Impending Tipping Point
sections.content: News that an agreement on the release date for the IPCC's upcoming 'Seventh Assessment Report on Climate Change' has fallen through suggests difficulties ahead for international climate response discussions [1, 3]. Furthermore, concerns are growing that the international community's response to the climate crisis could be delayed, as negotiations for the UN's 'Climate Response Guidelines' are also likely to reach a stalemate due to pressure from oil-producing nations, including China and Russia [4]. Moreover, with the global warming tipping point, which has been a concern for the past decade, now predicted to be crossed in just over a year, urgent warnings are being issued about the acceleration of climate change [22]. This situation once again underscores the importance and urgency of global cooperation.

sections.title: ⚠️ Deepening Impacts of the Climate Crisis and Widespread Damage Warnings
sections.content: The direct impacts of climate change are intensifying globally, with large-scale population displacement of up to 40 million people predicted in South Asia by 2050 due to climate change [2]. Domestically, Professor Shin Hyun-seok of Pusan National University emphasized the urgent need for a paradigm shift in flood defense, stating that 1,000-year frequency downpours are becoming a reality in the era of climate crisis [5]. Furthermore, subtle but serious changes are being detected across ecosystems, such as a decrease in protein in staple kitchen foods due to climate change [25], and humidity emerging as a critical factor for cave beetle survival [24]. The fact that nearly all homes destroyed by the 2019-20 'Black Summer' bushfires in New South Wales, Australia, were located within hazardous buffer zones clearly demonstrates the deadly threat that extreme weather events caused by climate change pose to human living environments [27].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Practices and Renewable Energy Transition Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts are actively underway to transition towards a carbon-neutral society. The Saehongcheon Rotary Club's carbon-neutral environmental cleanup activities and the Cheonan Youth Training Center's achievement of two awards for carbon neutrality contributions demonstrate the voluntary participation of local communities and youth [6, 7]. The Gyeonggi Provincial Office of Education has commenced the development of localized environmental education materials for practicing carbon neutrality in classrooms [8], and Cheonan City successfully hosted the '2nd Carbon Neutrality Forum 2026,' engaging citizens [9]. In the energy transition sector, 'Korea Power' (한국발전) is pushing for its launch next year through a reunification after 26 years, aiming to accelerate the shift towards renewable energy [11]. Furthermore, the Gyeongnam Provincial Office of Education is focusing on strengthening the management capabilities of new and renewable energy facilities in schools [13]. These are among the concrete movements being observed across the country to expand carbon neutrality and renewable energy.

sections.title: 🌱 Global Renewable Energy Expansion and Climate Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Internationally, efforts to expand renewable energy and adapt to climate change are also continuing. Qatar's share of renewable energy is projected to reach 25.9% by 2035, with solar power expected to drive this growth [10]. The commitment of various governments to renewable energy transition is evident, with candidates Lula and Bolsonaro competing over solar power expansion policies in Brazil's presidential election [16]. Furthermore, grid modernization and the spread of renewable energy are analyzed to drive the growth of the distribution-class surge arrester market and the instrument transformer mounting frame market until 2035 [15, 17]. Meanwhile, in addition to grants awarded for combating pollution and climate change [18], New Jersey State and Santa Barbara Airport are proactively engaging in climate adaptation efforts by soliciting public input on plans to protect and adapt key facilities from climate change [20, 21].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has once again highlighted the urgency of the climate crisis and the importance of international cooperation, while also shedding light on the positive changes and efforts underway in various countries and local communities. This concludes today's climate briefing.

summary.phenomenon: On May 21, 2024, southwestern Myanmar experienced forecasts of tropical thunderstorms, showers, and high temperatures up to 36 degrees Celsius, with monsoonal heat and humidity forming a massive convective column of water vapor extending up to 35,000 feet.
summary.cause: As the planet warms, airlines are grappling with the implications for air travel and passengers, leading to phenomena such as invisible turbulence.
summary.outlook: As the planet warms, airlines are contending with the impacts on air travel and passenger safety, particularly concerning invisible turbulence.
